context: The initial n is a nonnegative integer and the accumulator starts at res = 0. The function labeled recur(n, res) corresponds to tail_recur in the code.
description: The left column, “Descend,” lists the argument and accumulator. Every row in the right column, “Unwind,” returns the final sum unchanged. For a large n, the table shows the first and last calls in the figure, with ellipses for the intervening levels. A small n goes through only the arguments it needs. The depth is not fixed at 7. For n = 0, the function immediately returns the initial value 0.

frames.explanation: Start at recur(n, 0). At each step, first compute res + k, then call the next level with k−1 and the updated accumulator. At k = 1, the final term 1 still needs to be added. The next call, with k = 0, reaches the base case and returns the complete sum directly. Each call on the way back simply forwards the same result without further addition.
frames.title: Summing with tail recursion

result: Stack frames can be reused to bring stack space down to O(1) only if the runtime supports and enables tail-call optimization. Without the optimization, stack space remains O(n). Python does not support tail-call optimization by default.
summary: An accumulator lets each call do its addition before the recursive call and pass the result straight back on return.
